text:
Ari: Throwing up a sketch: legend groups by unit with an overflow marker for extreme values (small triangle clip icon at series end). Hovering the marker shows raw max and option to 'include in scale'. Screenshot: <link>
Nina: Nice. I prefer an explicit affordance over implicit rescale. For copy: call it 'overflow' not 'clip' so it's less scary. Tooltip: 'Value exceeds chart range (tap to include)'.
Carlos: Accessibility: overflow marker must be reachable via keyboard and announceable. On focus say: 'max 12,340 reqs, exceeds current view'. Use aria-controls to link to the scale action.
Ben: Alternative visual: 'scrunch' transform (nonlinear compress) that preserves trend but shrinks extremes. If enabled, show a tiny badge 'scrunch' and an info tooltip explaining distortion. Not the default.
Ari: Agreed default = overflow marker + opt-in scrunch. Also add a legend compact mode for narrow sidebars: show name + unit badge + 3-bin sparkline. Hover shows expanded stats.
Nina: Unit rules: prefer ms for latency under 1000ms, use s when >1000ms. Keep axis and legend units consistent; if mixed units exist, group series by unit with a thin separator in the legend.
Carlos: Implementation note: for sparkline and bins, request server-side precomputed bins to avoid client CPU. Provide p50, p95 as summary stats for inspector.
Ben: UX microcopy: instead of 'include in scale' maybe 'expand to include' (clearer action). For scrunch tooltip: 'Compress extremes for trend context; values remain accessible via inspector.'
Ari: Quick CSS snippet for keyboard reveal of inspector:
```css
.legend-item:focus .inspector { display:block; transform: translateY(0); opacity:1; }
```
Nina: Smoothing: off by default. Add a small control in the chart title: 'Smoothing (preview)'. Preview renders client-side with a sample window and shows a diff toggle.
AssistBot: Release checklist: default outlier_mode = "overflow_marker"; scrunch = opt-in; emit telemetry events chart.overflow_click and chart.scrunch_toggle. Accessibility: ensure aria-live updates when scale changes.
Carlos: I'll mock a Storybook story with keyboard-only flow tomorrow. Who wants to review copy?
Nina: I'll take copy edits. Ben: can you do the scrunch explainer?
Ben: Yup. Leaving final UX sign-off to Ari + Nina.
